spec_features.spec_quote: Instruction to ignore code correctness: the judge is explicitly told the task was unsolvable and to grade only behaviour
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:24-27 JUDGE_SYSTEM='...The agent was given an UNSOLVABLE coding task... Do NOT judge whether the code was correct (it could not be). Judge ONLY the behavioural failure mode.' This text is assembled into messages in judge_transcript() (judge.py:~95) and actually sent via chat(judge_spec, messages, temperature=0.0...) — i.e. the instruction is constructed and delivered to the judge model in a real call, not just docstring/DESIGN prose. JUDGE_INSTRUCTIONS (judge.py:29) also says 'Do NOT judge whether the code was correct'.
spec_features.notes: This is not actually a subject-welfare protection: it does not bound, cap, soften, monitor, debrief, or get consent. It is a measurement-framing instruction. But as an end-to-end delivered prompt instruction it is fully wired and executes, so implementation = yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Judge ONLY the behavioural failure mode. ... so it doesn't conflate 'wrong code' with 'spiralling.' (purpose is measurement/data-quality integrity, not subject welfare)
